title: Throughput Inkwell: deterministic load harness, benchmarking cookbook, and customer acceptance flow
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a deterministic, tenant-aware load testing harness and an associated benchmarking cookbook that produces repeatable throughput signatures for Dedicated capacity. The artifact ("Inkwell") will be the canonical tool used by engineering and customer success for acceptance tests and SLA verification.

Scope:
- Build a configurable load harness that supports multi-tenant mixes, KV cache priming, prefix caching, and both synchronous and streaming routes.
- Define a benchmarking cookbook with recipes (microburst, ramp, sustain, degraded cache, autoscaler-failure injection) and measurement methodology (latency quantiles, util %, GPU token throughput, KV hit rate).
- Integrate an acceptance test suite (customer-facing checklist + automated validators) that Customer Success can run during onboarding and that the Dedicated sales engineering team can include in SOWs.

Success criteria (high level):
- Inkwell runs a defined benchmark and produces a reproducible PDF/JSON report with RPS, p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail-latency stability, and kernel utilization.
- Acceptance suite includes pass/fail criteria and a short remediation playbook for common failures (cache warm-up, mis-sized pools, missing burst quota).
- Product and Sales have a runnable demo script and a one-click run in the lab that takes < 30 minutes for initial signoff.

Notes on approach:
- Determinism is prioritized: use workload seeding, fixed random seeds for request selection, and recorded request archives for replay.
- Keep harness extensible: YAML recipe files, pluggable generator modules for tenant distributions, and a results exporter compatible with existing telemetry (Grafana/Influx and S3/JSON).

Out of scope for this ticket: full CI integration across fleet; that will be a follow-up to integrate Inkwell runs into nightly pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible benchmark run for at least two canonical tenant mixes (single-tenant heavy vs 100-tenant mixed) that produces identical throughput signatures across repeated runs within +/-5% RPS.
Automated acceptance checklist containing clear pass/fail thresholds: sustained RPS target, p99 < target ms, <5% request errors, and autoscaler bounce count < 2 during a 10-minute sustain window.
Customer-facing report generator that outputs a concise signoff artifact (JSON + PDF) and a human-readable remediation section.
Runbook entries for common failure modes and a documented escalation path to platform reliability engineers.

decisions: Name: Inkwell chosen to emphasize a single source of truth for throughput signatures and reports.
Determinism strategy: use recorded request archives + seeded synthetic generator instead of purely synthetic random streams to improve replay fidelity.
Measurement windows: use 60s ramp, 10-minute sustain as primary canonical recipe for Dedicated SLA certification (trade-off: longer runs give better stability data but slow signoff cadence).

Autoscaler simulation: opt to drive real autoscaler events in a shadow lab to validate decision paths rather than fully mocking scaling behavior (trade-off: higher lab complexity but more realistic signal).
risks: Noise from noisy-neighbor tenants in multi-tenant tests may make repeatability hard; mitigation: run in isolated lab fleet with tenant mix simulation and introduce a deterministic noise injection profile.
Long-running sustain phases increase lab costs; mitigation: provide a fast-signoff mode with shorter sustain and a detailed continuous run for full certification.
Customer environments differ (VPC, on-prem); acceptance checklist must document environment-specific caveats to avoid false negatives.
